title: targets becomes capabilities
decision: Rename targets to capabilities in the schema, the hand-written validator, DecisionTimeline, and all 45 records. The field keeps its shape: a non-empty array of unique hierarchical capability IDs. The rename is part of the same migration pass as the flattening, so no record is touched twice.
context: The targets field was named for what it did under the promotion model: it named the expected promotion destination, made the affected boundary reviewable at G1, and was the thing Archive reconciled against delivered behaviour before copying the record. None of those three jobs survives the flat model. What the field does afterwards is state which capabilities a decision applies to, and that value is both the rendering key for Feature pages and the retrieval key for an agent looking for the decisions that bind a piece of code. docs/agents/domain.md already defines each value as a hierarchical capability or sub-capability ID, so the vocabulary exists and the field name is the only thing out of step with it.

alternatives.reason: It states the relation more explicitly, but says nothing about what the values are; capabilities names the vocabulary the values come from, which is the thing a reader needs.
Too strong for the whole set: some decisions constrain a capability without governing it, and the field has one meaning for every record.
Already taken twice in this repository, by commit scope and by Change scope, both of which appear in the same documents as decision records.
It would keep a name whose meaning was the promotion destination after promotion is gone, which is exactly the kind of stale name this Change is removing elsewhere.

consequences: The schema, the validator, DecisionTimeline, and 45 records change together; a half-applied rename fails validation loudly rather than rendering wrongly.
Records published on the blueprint-changes store branch keep the old field name and are read through the compatibility layer.
revisitTriggers: A decision needs to name something that is not a capability, such as a package or a route.
